sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: All customer-facing transfer notifications trigger an SMS dispatch event to the primary registered mobile number.

sections.heading: Retry Policy
sections.content: SMS notifications automatically retry 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) before marking delivery as failed. If all retries fail, an alert is published to the notifications dead-letter queue.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.content: Verify provider gateway connectivity and check whether the recipient number is on the National Do Not Disturb (DND) registry.

sections.heading: Domestic Beneficiaries
sections.content: Domestic beneficiaries require a valid 10-18 digit account number and an 11-character Indian Financial System Code (IFSC). Cooling period is 30 minutes with a ₹50,000 transaction limit during cooling.

sections.heading: International Beneficiaries
sections.content: To add an international beneficiary, navigate to Settings > Beneficiary Management > Add International. Enter the recipient's IBAN or Account Number, bank SWIFT/BIC code, destination country, bank physical address, and remittance purpose code (e.g. S0101 for education, S0102 for software services). Approval requires document verification and completes within 4 business hours.

sections.heading: Security Verification
sections.content: A one-time passcode (OTP) is sent to the registered mobile number to confirm beneficiary addition.

docs.title: Standard Operating Procedure: Same-Day Transfer Cutoff Windows
docs.author: payments-ops@bank.org

sections.heading: Cutoff Schedule
sections.content: Same-day domestic transfers (RTGS/NEFT) must be submitted before 16:00 Indian Standard Time (IST, UTC+5:30). Any transfer initiated at or after 16:00 IST is rejected or queued for the next business day clearing cycle.

sections.heading: Timezone Handling
sections.content: All business logic evaluating operating hours must calculate the current time in Asia/Kolkata timezone (IST) regardless of the server or container's system clock (which runs in UTC).

docs.title: Fee Schedule and Tier Calculation Guide
docs.author: finance-billing@bank.org

sections.heading: Standard Tier Transfers
sections.content: The standard tier transfer fee is strictly 1.25% (0.0125) of the principal transfer amount, rounded to 2 decimal places using standard financial decimal arithmetic. Calculations must use high-precision Decimal types to prevent fractional cent/paisa drift.

sections.heading: Fee Caps and Minimums
sections.content: Minimum fee is ₹1.00; maximum fee is ₹500.00 for standard retail transfers.

docs.title: Transfer Limits and Risk Controls Policy
docs.author: risk-compliance@bank.org

sections.heading: Daily Cumulative Limits
sections.content: The daily cumulative transfer limit for standard retail accounts is ₹1,00,000. Transfers exceeding this limit are blocked. Transfers equal to ₹1,00,000 are permitted and must not be rejected.

sections.heading: Per-Transaction Limits
sections.content: Maximum single transaction limit is ₹1,00,000 for retail tier.

sections.heading: Header Specification
sections.content: Mutating endpoints (such as POST /api/transfers) accept an Idempotency-Key header. Header inspection must be case-insensitive (Idempotency-Key or idempotency-key). An atomic distributed lock must be acquired before ledger debit to guarantee zero duplicate execution.
